sources.title: Ung Lab
sources.text: Ung Translational Neurophysiology Lab Our research team is focused on the development and deployment of quantitative and artificial intelligence tools to improve the efficiency and efficacy of management of neurological diseases. Our current projects include: Understanding current barriers to the management of seizures in the inpatient setting Development and testing of automated EEG analysis tools including seizure detection Identification of neurophysiologic biomarkers in epilepsy and other disease states Meet our Team !

sources.title: Our Team
sources.text: Principal Investigator Hoameng Ung MD PhD Dr. Ung is an Assistant Clinical Professor of Neurology at UC San Diego Department of Neurosciences, Comprehensive Epilepsy Center . His research has harnessed the power of machine learning to uncover EEG biomarkers associated with epilepsy and other neurological phenomena. Having completed a residency and fellowship in Neurology and Epilepsy at UC San Diego, Dr. Ung is a practicing neurologist, providing care to patients in both hospital and outpatient settings. These patients motivate his commitment to advancing clinical practice and improving patient outcomes through technological innovation. Google scholar LinkedIn Members Solana Fernandez Solana is a graduate student pursuing a master’s in Bioengineering. Having joined the lab in summer 2025, she presently works on LLM-driven classification of clinical EEG records and validation of seizure detection algorithms. Previously, she performed acute electrophysiological recordings of the macaque hippocampus at the University of Washington to investigate learning and memory mechanisms. In her spare time, she enjoys weightlifting, boxing, and yoga. Remey Song Remey is an undergraduate student at UC San Diego majoring in Neurobiology with a minor in Philosophy on the pre-med track. She joined the lab in September 2025 and is currently investigating EEG biomarkers associated with delayed cerebral ischemia following subarachnoid hemorrhage. Previously, she researched time-of-day-dependent serotonergic chemosensitivities of respiratory responses in mouse models of Sudden Unexpected Death in Epilepsy. Previous Members: Carter Tran Emily Xie Ankey Zhu Jessica Li
